text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- United Malays National Organisation headquarters has released the list of 185 candidates qualified to contest in the party's elections next months.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad in Lisbon, Portugal, confirmed that Malaysia will host a leg of the Formula One race starting from 1999.

-- Businessman and MP Joseph Chong may challenge Gerakan party president, Lim Keng Yaik, for the top post in party elections on Oct 5, a Chong aide said. Gerakan is a key component party of the ruling National Front coalition in northern Penang state.

-- Initial public offerings will continue to attract punters as long as bumper premiums are to be reaped. So far this year, most newly listed companies have posted 100 percent or bigger premiums on their first day of trading.
-- About 300 companies will make up the initial list of a proposed Islamic Index on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, said Deputy Finance Minister Affifuddin Omar.
-- The government must halt an exercise to legalise foreign workers who are in the country illegally as it has created more problems than it solved, said Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers.

-- Central bank, Bank Negara will pursue vigorous policy initiatives to quickly develop the insurance sector as a key component of the financial services sector, Governor Ahmad Mohamad Don said in an interview.
